$comment: Lighthouse for the doc web. Two tickets carried a Lighthouse number in
their acceptance and nobody measured one, because it needs a served
site — so the figures that existed came from curl, and a transfer size
is not a score. Without a score there is no way to say whether the
site is getting slower.
Measured against the built site served locally rather than against the
Vercel preview. A job that waits for a bot's comment to appear is a job
that fails for reasons no reader can act on; this one measures the same
artefact and needs no secret. What it does NOT see is the CDN's
compression and caching, so Performance here reads LOWER than the live
site — which is the safe direction for a budget to be wrong in.
Three addresses, because they are three different shapes: the entry
point, a component page with a live demo, and a guide that is mostly
prose and one long table.
THREE RUNS, not one. A single run on a shared runner moved a page by
ten points between two commits that could not account for it, which is
worse than no number: it invites a hunt for a regression that is only
the runner having a busy minute. Lighthouse reports the median run, so
three is the smallest count that has one. It costs about two extra
minutes and buys a figure that can be compared with the last one --
and this check becomes required, so a number that swings by ten would
block pull requests at random.
